map.KSUID（K-Sortable Unique ID）把「可按时间排序」与「全局: KSUID (K-Sortable Unique ID) combines time-sortability with global uniqueness: the first 4 bytes are a big-endian Unix timestamp in seconds and the last 16 bytes are a cryptographically random payload. In byte form it is 20 bytes; in string form it is encoded as 27 base62 characters. Because the timestamp occupies the high-order bytes, comparing KSUIDs as strings yields generation order, so they work directly as database primary keys or log sort keys while avoiding the way auto-increment IDs reveal business volume. Collision probability is guaranteed by the 16 random bytes (a 2¹²⁸ space) and is negligible in practice.
